design: The filter_neighborhood.json experiment fixes one slate of up to seven uniformly sampled distinct one-exchanges and an F prefix. Test candidate-pool draw sensitivity by adding two independent slates; this supplement was fixed after the first slate predictions were sealed and before the additional slates were constructed. Keep tasks, model seeds, guard, anchor, proposal and outer rows, tolerance and all policies fixed. Previously computed supports can be reused only with the identical fold, support and training recipe.
sampling: Use exactly the filter-neighborhood generator with the first entropy integer replaced by the designated replicate seed. Fully enumerate when at most seven exchanges exist. Keep all three draws, their pairwise candidate-set Jaccard similarities, and counts of folds with identical or overlapping pools. Do not replace repeated slates. Seal new nominations and probabilities before scoring them.
estimand: First estimate each policy and full-minus-ordinal outcome on each draw. Then average draws within fold, folds within source, and weight sources equally and separately by panel. Primary endpoint guarded U with breach risk alongside; point and F prefix and exact within-slate uniform are controls. Give per-draw results, source-level range and paired source bootstrap with draws kept together. Additional random draws are not independent datasets or outer samples. State which parts remain conditioned on a single seed.
